nodes.norm_label: object storage: r2 for public media, supabase storage for private docs, s3 dropped
nodes.rationale: No other AWS footprint (Railway + Supabase + Clerk); R2 has no egress fee for storefront images.

nodes.label: vX.Y.Z version scheme
nodes.rationale: X = major/epic (breaking, coordinated platform shifts), Y = backward-compatible feature releases, Z = fixes/patches; pre-release approval date must be on or before release date for audit trail.

nodes.label: Owner-filtered write: where {id, chefProfileId: null}
nodes.rationale: Putting the owner filter in the update/delete where clause leaves no gap between the ownership check and the write; on P2025 one lookup decides between 404 and 403 CONTENT_NOT_OWNED.

nodes.label: params: line contract
nodes.rationale: Each template header declares its params; the backend mailer method must send exactly those params, and tests check templates use nothing else.

nodes.label: Brevo shared email layout
nodes.rationale: Shared shell (Lab's Food header, footer with contact@labsfood.fr, <!-- title --> and <!-- content --> slots); light color scheme only, MSO conditional table for Outlook.

nodes.label: Application approved email (BREVO_TPL_APPLICATION_APPROVED)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName dashboardUrl. Welcomes a verified batch cooker.

nodes.label: Application received email (BREVO_TPL_APPLICATION_RECEIVED)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName reference signInUrl expiresAt. Carries the only way into the new account (one-time sign-in link); never remove signInUrl.

nodes.label: Application received admin email (BREVO_TPL_APPLICATION_RECEIVED_ADMIN)
nodes.rationale: params: reference applicationId name city adminUrl. Sent to admin inbox, also on reapply; name and city come from the public form.

nodes.label: Application rejected email (BREVO_TPL_APPLICATION_REJECTED)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName reason allowReapplyAfter. allowReapplyAfter null means reapply at once; account stays; documents deleted 3 months after decision.

nodes.label: Changes requested email (BREVO_TPL_CHANGES_REQUESTED)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName message documentLabels dossierUrl. Admin-written message shown as written; documentLabels never empty.

nodes.label: Chef suspended email (BREVO_TPL_CHEF_SUSPENDED)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName documentLabel dossierUrl. Only time the platform takes a storefront offline without a human decision (mandatory document expired); lifted on upload of an updated version.

nodes.label: Contact received admin email (BREVO_TPL_CONTACT_RECEIVED_ADMIN)
nodes.rationale: params: name email phone subject message site inboxUrl. Internal heads-up when a public contact form is sent; Reply-To is the visitor.

nodes.label: Contact reply email (BREVO_TPL_CONTACT_REPLY)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName subject reply originalMessage. Admin's answer from the console, sent as written, quoting the visitor's message; Reply-To is the team.

nodes.label: Content suspended email (BREVO_TPL_CONTENT_SUSPENDED)
nodes.rationale: params: kind title reason reasonCode menus recipesUrl. Dish or menu takedown; copyright/inappropriate-content takedowns also delete the dish photo.

nodes.label: Document expiring email (BREVO_TPL_DOCUMENT_EXPIRING)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName documentLabel expiresOn daysLeft dossierUrl. daysLeft is the notice threshold crossed (60, 30 or 7), hence 'd'ici'.

nodes.label: Document rejected email (BREVO_TPL_DOCUMENT_REJECTED)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName documentLabel reason dossierUrl. Admin-written reason shown as written.

nodes.label: New message email (BREVO_TPL_NEW_MESSAGE)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName senderName unreadCount conversationUrl. Sent by the messaging job after 10 min unread, once per burst; never quotes the message, which would bypass masking of contact details.

nodes.label: Sign-in link email (BREVO_TPL_SIGN_IN_LINK)
nodes.rationale: params: firstName signInUrl expiresAt. Sent when an admin re-sends a sign-in link; never remove signInUrl.

nodes.label: Source recipe changed email (BREVO_TPL_SOURCE_CHANGED)
nodes.rationale: params: dishName recipesUrl. Lab's Food source proposal changed on a sensitive point (allergens, diets, recipe country); the chef's dish is untouched.

nodes.label: signInUrl invariant
nodes.rationale: APPLICATION_RECEIVED and SIGN_IN_LINK must keep href=params.signInUrl: it is the candidate's only way into their account.

nodes.label: chef_profiles table
nodes.rationale: May later converge with TeamMember modeling and chef assignment on bookings.

nodes.norm_label: fiscal attestations per provider (json, no pdf)
nodes.rationale: The chef is the prestataire so one attestation per provider; tax year decided by paidAt; legal PDF template pending.

nodes.label: SAP declaration (type A NOVA / type B cooperative)
nodes.norm_label: sap declaration (type a nova / type b cooperative)
nodes.rationale: URSSAF/CRCESU statuses are not chef-writable: no self-habilitation.

nodes.norm_label: 4-step reservation flow (meals, info, stripe payment, confirmation)

nodes.norm_label: evolution register - payments (stripe cb, connect, sap/sepa)

nodes.rationale: Only approving the candidature grants is_verified; chefs cannot self-verify.

nodes.label: ChefDossierCron daily job (expiry warnings, suspension, purge)
nodes.norm_label: chefdossiercron daily job (expiry warnings, suspension, purge)
nodes.rationale: Runs in every replica if scaled; steps are idempotent; move to a queue or advisory lock at scale.

nodes.rationale: Self-declared profile data that carries no Stripe secrets.

nodes.label: Unvetted chef gap (is_active / is_verified unread)
nodes.rationale: Now money-bearing: an unvetted chef who completes Stripe Connect onboarding is payable.

nodes.norm_label: post /bookings closed (501): bookings come from accepted offers

nodes.label: Commission arithmetic (bps, VAT on rounded HT, clamped, frozen)
nodes.norm_label: commission arithmetic (bps, vat on rounded ht, clamped, frozen)
nodes.rationale: HT + VAT === TTC; clamp so a misconfigured rate cannot fail payments; zero fee omitted; rates frozen on the commissions row so history is never rewritten.

nodes.label: Stripe Connect destination charge
nodes.rationale: Commission withheld atomically as application_fee_amount: no second debit, no payout job; backend never sees card details.

nodes.label: PaymentIntent reuse (double-click idempotency)
nodes.rationale: Returns the live pending intent; drops unconfirmable intents; 409 if Stripe already settled it.

nodes.label: Refunds as passive bookkeeping (commission not clawed back)
nodes.norm_label: refunds as passive bookkeeping (commission not clawed back)

nodes.label: payments 1:N bookings (retryable attempts)
nodes.rationale: A failed card attempt must be retryable with a fresh PaymentIntent.

nodes.label: One .html per BREVO_TPL_* plus layout.html, loaded by templates.mjs
nodes.norm_label: one .html per brevo_tpl_* plus layout.html, loaded by templates.mjs
nodes.rationale: Native .html import fails with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION on Node 20 and 26, so readFileSync with import.meta.url; file name equals env var so no mapping table; output must stay byte-identical to the previous JS literals.

nodes.label: Brevo email templates README
nodes.rationale: The repo is the source of truth for transactional email text; Brevo holds a copy kept in sync by upload.mjs.

nodes.label: Brevo template security rules
nodes.rationale: Only params declared on the params: line, no contact.*, no unescaped output (|safe, autoescape off, raw), href/src only https:/mailto:/server-built *Url params, only *Url params inside HTML attributes because names/cities/dish titles/admin reasons are typed by people (some on a public form).

nodes.label: Upload digest drift detection
nodes.rationale: Every upload stamps an 'uploaded <digest>' comment before </body>; --check uses it to tell a repo change from a Brevo editor edit, and --update refuses to overwrite a Brevo edit without --force.

nodes.label: Document-type enum in Swagger (DOCUMENT_TYPES derived from DOCUMENT_LABEL)
nodes.norm_label: document-type enum in swagger (document_types derived from document_label)
nodes.rationale: One source, kebab-case, in family order (blocking, conditional, recommended); behaviour unchanged, an unknown value is still 404.

nodes.label: ECC review chain: tdd-guide, database-reviewer, typescript-reviewer, security-reviewer
nodes.norm_label: ecc review chain: tdd-guide, database-reviewer, typescript-reviewer, security-reviewer
nodes.rationale: database-reviewer gates every step with a migration; security-reviewer closes chains that touch a trust boundary (ownership rule, verification gate, public reads, uploads, recipe exposure); CRITICAL and HIGH findings fixed before each milestone commit.

nodes.norm_label: flow-02 m2: a chef can publish a dish

nodes.norm_label: flow-02 m3: a chef can publish a week

nodes.norm_label: flow-02 m4: a chef can start from lab's food

nodes.norm_label: flow-02 m5: the public page lists cooks, not dishes

nodes.label: FLOW-02 M6: Admins can moderate after the fact
nodes.norm_label: flow-02 m6: admins can moderate after the fact

nodes.norm_label: flow-02 m8: a prestation leaves its documents (fiche recette, shopping list, culinary map)

nodes.label: Offers: content prepared for one chef, owned only on acceptance
nodes.norm_label: offers: content prepared for one chef, owned only on acceptance
nodes.rationale: Lets Lab's Food build a menu for a batch cooker without imposing it (section 6, nothing is imposed); accepting transfers the row itself since no other chef needs the original; declining leaves it with Lab's Food.

nodes.label: Lab's Food suggestions (unowned, offered to no one, visible to every chef)
nodes.norm_label: lab's food suggestions (unowned, offered to no one, visible to every chef)

nodes.label: PRD: plats, menus, publication et moderation (FLOW-02)
nodes.norm_label: prd: plats, menus, publication et moderation (flow-02)

nodes.label: Derived row kinds: chef dish, offer, suggestion, Lab's Food draft
nodes.norm_label: derived row kinds: chef dish, offer, suggestion, lab's food draft
nodes.rationale: Never stored: derived from chef_profile_id, offered_to_chef_profile_id and published status, so the kind cannot drift from the data.

nodes.label: Adoption: idempotent copy with lineage and audit-log consent
nodes.norm_label: adoption: idempotent copy with lineage and audit-log consent
nodes.rationale: Previews carry no ingredients or steps and non-owner chefs have no recipe access, so adoption is what hands the recipe over; the original stays unowned so one chef adopting never takes it from another; idempotent per (chef, source) to absorb double clicks and dishes shared between menus.

nodes.label: Shopping lists computed deterministically from structured ingredient lists
nodes.norm_label: shopping lists computed deterministically from structured ingredient lists
nodes.rationale: recipe.ingredients is validated as a list of {name, qty, unit, aisle} on every write path (legacy /admin/meals accepted only an object), so scaling, dedup by (name, unit) and grouping by aisle is arithmetic not inference; AI-generated lists are out of scope; chef corrections survive recalculation.

nodes.label: Direct publication, moderation after the fact
nodes.norm_label: direct publication, moderation after the fact
nodes.rationale: Decided 20/09/2026; it makes the automatic checks the only barrier before a dish is public, so those checks are blocking (section 3.3).

nodes.label: Explicit allergen declaration (allergens or allergensNone; custom values never count)
nodes.norm_label: explicit allergen declaration (allergens or allergensnone; custom values never count)
nodes.rationale: An empty array cannot distinguish no allergens from not filled in; a free-text value like sarrasin must not satisfy the gate while the 14 regulated allergens stay unanswered.

nodes.label: Publishing a menu publishes its draft dishes, all or nothing
nodes.norm_label: publishing a menu publishes its draft dishes, all or nothing
nodes.rationale: Removes eight separate publications for an adopted 7-dish menu; section 3.4 already forbids a published menu containing a draft dish; lifts draft only, never suspended, so a moderation decision is not bypassed.

nodes.label: GET /menus/current deprecated, every call logged
nodes.rationale: No consumer exists in either frontend and GET /menus/week supersedes it; logging surfaces any outside consumer in Railway before removal.

nodes.label: Recipes versioned; a prestation pins the version it was cooked from
nodes.norm_label: recipes versioned; a prestation pins the version it was cooked from
nodes.rationale: Settles section 9.2: the fiche the client received and the one the API serves always agree and a dispute about what was cooked is answerable; the fiche flags a newer version with pinned and current numbers; re-pinning before the prestation is audited and regenerates the shopping list.

nodes.label: Safety-relevant edit to a suggestion flags its copies source-changed
nodes.norm_label: safety-relevant edit to a suggestion flags its copies source-changed
nodes.rationale: Copies are insulated from bad edits but also from corrections; an edit to allergens, diets or country flags each copy, notifies its chef and queues it for review, never auto-applied nor auto-suspended because expiry stays the only unattended takedown.

nodes.label: suspended status valid only for chef-owned rows (CHECK constraint)
nodes.norm_label: suspended status valid only for chef-owned rows (check constraint)
nodes.rationale: Keeps archived (Lab's Food retired it) and suspended (a chef was moderated) from blurring into one column.

nodes.label: Vitrine order: monthly-seeded rotation above a relevance floor
nodes.norm_label: vitrine order: monthly-seeded rotation above a relevance floor
nodes.rationale: Ordering decides who receives demand; rating-first would entrench early arrivals; one order per calendar month matches the Vitrine du mois cadence and keeps pagination stable; chefs with no menu for the week are listed last and marked rather than hidden.

nodes.label: J-2 contact release (48h before a confirmed booking)
nodes.norm_label: j-2 contact release (48h before a confirmed booking)
nodes.rationale: Nothing is stored: moving or cancelling the booking changes the answer.

nodes.label: api service (apps/Dockerfile, port 8000)
nodes.rationale: Docker-local DB defaults overridable with DOCKER_* vars; integration secrets default to empty.

nodes.label: redis service (redis:7-alpine)
nodes.rationale: Messaging rate limit and realtime fan-out; nothing durable is kept in it.

nodes.label: local-dev api service
nodes.rationale: No Redis service and no REDIS_URL here, so rate limit and realtime fan-out stay in-process.

nodes.label: labsfood-web service (port 3007)
nodes.rationale: Gets BREVO_SMTP_USER/PASS, BREVO_FROM_EMAIL and CONTACT_TO_EMAIL for its own contact email path.

nodes.label: Brevo transactional email
nodes.rationale: Transactional notifications.

nodes.label: Clerk auth
nodes.rationale: OAuth2/sessions; API validates Bearer tokens; Clerk stays the auth source, no /auth/register routes.

nodes.label: Cloudflare R2
nodes.rationale: Public S3-compatible storage for dish photos, chosen for no egress fee.

nodes.label: Cronofy
nodes.rationale: Chef availability / scheduling.

nodes.label: Google Maps API
nodes.rationale: Zones, routing when needed.

nodes.label: In-house messaging module
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL + REST + /ws WebSocket for client-chef and support conversations; not an integration, lives in modules/messaging.

nodes.label: NestJS 11 + Fastify API
nodes.rationale: Monolithic REST + OpenAPI API on Node.js 20, shared by all Lab's Food web clients.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 16
nodes.rationale: Supabase-hosted or local Docker.

nodes.label: Prisma 7.6 ORM
nodes.rationale: Target ORM replacing interim TypeORM; apps/prisma.config.ts + apps/prisma/schema.prisma.

nodes.label: Railway hosting
nodes.rationale: API + Postgres + Redis containers.

nodes.label: Redis 7 (optional)
nodes.rationale: Messaging rate limit and WebSocket fan-out between instances; without REDIS_URL both stay in-process.

nodes.label: client / chef / admin roles
nodes.rationale: Admin authorization via AdminGuard plus persisted UserRole.ADMIN.

nodes.label: Stripe Connect destination charges
nodes.rationale: Platform commission as application_fee_amount, chef Express onboarding, SEPA commission mandates, POST /webhooks/stripe.

nodes.label: Supabase Storage
nodes.rationale: Private storage for chef KYC documents.

nodes.label: local-dev full-stack docker-compose.yml
nodes.rationale: Full-stack local orchestration for 4 LabsFood services + Postgres; must be copied to the parent folder holding the cloned repos side by side; secrets from one root .env.

nodes.label: Backend domain naming decisions
nodes.rationale: Keep 'bookings' over spec 'Reservation'; legacy 'provider' migrated to 'chef'; Clerk instead of spec email/password JWT; Prisma instead of interim TypeORM.

nodes.label: Status & badge color mapping per domain
nodes.norm_label: status & badge color mapping per domain

nodes.label: Booking status pending->confirmed driven by payment webhook
nodes.norm_label: booking status pending->confirmed driven by payment webhook
nodes.rationale: The API never confirms a booking on the client's word; a failed payment leaves it pending for retry; shopping/cooking/delivered unimplemented.

nodes.label: bookings aggregate (spec 'reservation')

nodes.label: Clerk BAPI email auto-verification risk
nodes.rationale: Nothing proves address ownership, so typo'd/disposable addresses reach users; flagged as pre-payments risk.

nodes.rationale: Guards read the DB, not Clerk metadata.

nodes.rationale: Next.js owns sign-in and sessions via Clerk FAPI; the API owns sign-up, JWT verification, webhooks, GET /me upsert and Postgres RBAC.

nodes.label: Route selects the role, never the request body
nodes.norm_label: route selects the role, never the request body
nodes.rationale: role is absent from every DTO so forbidNonWhitelisted returns 400; admin has no public surface.

nodes.rationale: API uses Prisma via SUPABASE_DB_URL, never the Supabase JS client; Supabase RLS does not apply on the API path.

nodes.label: Login/refresh/logout out of scope (Clerk owns sessions)
nodes.norm_label: login/refresh/logout out of scope (clerk owns sessions)

nodes.label: Batch cookers in the back office (LF-0164, GET /admin/chefs)
nodes.norm_label: batch cookers in the back office (lf-0164, get /admin/chefs)
nodes.rationale: Built on chef_profiles, not candidatures, so pre-FLOW-01 profiles are listed; STATE_WHERE is the single definition of online/offline/suspended/pending for filter, counts and rows; deleted accounts never listed.

nodes.rationale: One client account per row; clientProfile is null until the client saves preferences.

nodes.rationale: Admin side mirrors every client-side feature; the UI is complete but runs on mock data pending backend wiring.

nodes.norm_label: adminsettings singleton (vat, tax credit rate, currency)

nodes.norm_label: client and chef space switcher (dual-role account)
nodes.rationale: Feasible and cheap on the backend: both profiles are already optional 1:1 relations and authorisation is profile-based, so no migration; what blocks it is one guard and frontend routing on a single role. Decision pending, recorded as ponytail debt.

nodes.label: Compensating Clerk user delete on submission transaction failure
nodes.norm_label: compensating clerk user delete on submission transaction failure
nodes.rationale: Prevents an orphaned Clerk identity with no database row, and an address that could no longer apply.

nodes.label: Analysis: one account, two spaces (client and chef switcher)
nodes.norm_label: analysis: one account, two spaces (client and chef switcher)

nodes.norm_label: rework #37: the account exists from candidature submission

nodes.label: Self-dealing guard (no booking, quoting or paying your own chef profile)
nodes.norm_label: self-dealing guard (no booking, quoting or paying your own chef profile)
nodes.rationale: With URSSAF avance immediate the client gets a 50% tax credit on the amount paid, so booking yourself is a tax-credit fraud surface; must ship with the switcher, and closes a hole that already exists since booking creation never checks client != chef.

nodes.label: Clerk user.deleted anonymisation (deleted_at tombstone)
nodes.rationale: A deletion blocked by bookings (P2003) anonymises the users row instead of retrying: bookings keep address_line and notes under GDPR art. 17(3)(b) because services-a-la-personne billing (tax certificate, URSSAF avance immediate) needs the client identity for years; the anonymised row resists a late user.updated, a hard-deleted one does not.

nodes.label: Security requirements for public account creation
nodes.norm_label: security requirements for public account creation
nodes.rationale: An email that already has an account must never gain a chef profile from an unauthenticated request (account-takeover path); throttle with ThrottlerGuard; no account enumeration; Clerk verifies the email before the account can act; privileged fields kept out of the body via forbidNonWhitelisted.

nodes.label: Signed-in reapply (POST /me/chef-application/reapply)
nodes.rationale: Public submission now refuses an email that already has an account, so without a signed-in path every refusal would become permanent despite the reapply date.

nodes.label: Client-to-chef self-promotion removed; PATCH /me/chef-profile is update-only
nodes.norm_label: client-to-chef self-promotion removed; patch /me/chef-profile is update-only
nodes.rationale: Two routes to becoming a chef, one unvetted, contradicted the premise; the route survives for verified self-edit only, a client gets 404 and a candidate 403.

nodes.label: OpenAPI check script (NestFactory preview, no database)
nodes.norm_label: openapi check script (nestfactory preview, no database)
nodes.rationale: Swagger config moved from main.ts to src/swagger.ts buildOpenApiDocument(app) so the document builds without starting the server; fails on any operation lacking summary, description or success response, a {type} without enum, or a remaining /content path.

nodes.label: Swagger pass on every route (summary, description, examples, error codes)
nodes.norm_label: swagger pass on every route (summary, description, examples, error codes)
nodes.rationale: Tags registered in the user's path through the product; admin routes get their own sections, with tags moved from class to method because Swagger merges class and method tags; enum values listed in lifecycle or family order with one line each.

nodes.rationale: Documentation pass must not change behaviour; questionable behaviour is documented as it is and listed for the user to decide.

nodes.label: Optional Brevo and R2 configuration degrades gracefully
nodes.norm_label: optional brevo and r2 configuration degrades gracefully
nodes.rationale: An email without a template id is a logged no-op and a photo route without R2 answers 503 PHOTOS_UNAVAILABLE, the same degradation FLOW-01 uses.

nodes.label: Standing rules: read-only DB, commit only when asked, no attribution, frontends read-only
nodes.norm_label: standing rules: read-only db, commit only when asked, no attribution, frontends read-only
nodes.rationale: User rules: never write to the database or apply a migration unasked (Docker Postgres unreliable, prefer Supabase read-only tooling); push only to the named remote branch; batchcooking-web and labsfood-web are read-only, stale docs are reported not edited; ponytail shortest correct diff.

nodes.label: Verification gate: build, jest, lint checked by exit code
nodes.norm_label: verification gate: build, jest, lint checked by exit code
nodes.rationale: Checked by exit code because a piped tail once hid a failure; SUPABASE_DB_URL and SUPABASE_DB_MIGRATION_URL set to any postgres URL since the prisma config requires them though nothing connects.

nodes.label: Where the FLOW-02 spec is followed loosely
nodes.norm_label: where the flow-02 spec is followed loosely
nodes.rationale: A suggestion is an unowned Lab's Food row, so /admin/meals and /admin/menus serve it rather than a second endpoint (two sources of truth); {data, meta} pagination kept for consistency; a mission is a booking; card fields without a table are null; sessionFromCents is the cheapest active service offer since commission lives on the payments branch; recipes pinned on first use via pinRecipes because POST /bookings answers 501.

nodes.label: FLOW-02 known limits (ponytail notes)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately left: GET /menus/week and the moderation queue filter and page in memory; sessionFromCents ignores commission (lives on the payments branch); booking creation should call pinRecipes; a deleted dish leaves its R2 photo; anonymised chef candidature and identity documents kept until an end of contract is modelled.

nodes.label: audit_log: compliance journal and debugging trail
nodes.norm_label: audit_log: compliance journal and debugging trail
nodes.rationale: Railway log retention is short and cannot be queried by candidature; audit_log records reads, decisions, approvals, suspensions and failures, keyed by x-request-id.

nodes.label: Auth testing without Clerk (sk_test_placeholder decodes JWT without JWKS)
nodes.norm_label: auth testing without clerk (sk_test_placeholder decodes jwt without jwks)

nodes.label: In-house messaging (chef_client and support conversations)
nodes.rationale: Stream was dropped; one conversation per (client, chef profile) pair; one writer (MessagingService.postMessage); a conversation the caller is not part of is 404; writable while a booking is pending or confirmed and 14 days after completion.

nodes.label: Redis optional (in-process fallback for messaging rate limit and events)
nodes.norm_label: redis optional (in-process fallback for messaging rate limit and events)
nodes.rationale: With REDIS_URL the 20/minute send limit and events are shared between instances; without it both are in-process, fine for one instance and wrong for two.

nodes.rationale: Containerising LF-BackEnd, batchcooking-web, labsfood-web and admin-dashboard removes Node/npm version drift between repos; orchestration files live in LF-BackEnd because the parent folder is not a git repo.

nodes.norm_label: public railway domain vs private railway.internal hostname
nodes.rationale: *.railway.internal is reachable only service-to-service inside Railway; browsers, Swagger and frontends must use the public domain https://lf-api.labsfood.fr.

nodes.rationale: A re-serialised JSON body would fail Svix/Stripe signature verification.

nodes.norm_label: opaque candidate token machinery removed (application-token, guard, resend-link)

nodes.norm_label: retention purge on the flow-01 section 8 schedule

nodes.norm_label: service-a-la-personne regime (identity, registration and insurance evidence)

nodes.norm_label: flow-01 success metrics (funnel completion, 48h decision sla, zero unevidenced chefs)

nodes.label: Automatic-suspension episode (chef_profiles.auto_suspended_at)
nodes.rationale: auto_suspended_at IS NOT NULL AND is_active means live on an unreviewed document; those dossiers sort first in the admin queue; validating clears it, refusing takes the chef offline; an admin-deactivated chef is never auto-reactivated.

nodes.label: PRD: batch cooker onboarding (candidature, KYC, admin validation)
nodes.norm_label: prd: batch cooker onboarding (candidature, kyc, admin validation)

nodes.label: Admin verification bypass closed (PATCH /admin/chefs/:id/verification answers 409)
nodes.rationale: Once every candidate holds a chef profile, setting isVerified directly would verify a candidate with no document check; refused unless the candidature is approved, and isActive refused on an unverified profile.

nodes.label: Submitting a candidature creates a browse-only account
nodes.norm_label: submitting a candidature creates a browse-only account
nodes.rationale: Decided 21/09/2026, reversing FLOW-01 section 1: the candidate works signed in from a dashboard instead of through a scoped link, which removes the candidate token, its resend endpoint and account creation at approval. A refused candidate keeps the account and reapplies from it.

nodes.label: Answers correctable until decision, locked once a validated document proves them
nodes.norm_label: answers correctable until decision, locked once a validated document proves them
nodes.rationale: Otherwise a typo needs a refusal and reapplication; the lock keeps each admin decision tied to the answer it was made against. Email and consent never change.

nodes.label: Daily in-process scheduled job for expiry, suspension and retention
nodes.norm_label: daily in-process scheduled job for expiry, suspension and retention
nodes.rationale: No queue infrastructure exists and none is warranted at this scale; known ceiling is double-firing under multiple API replicas, mitigated by making the job idempotent.

nodes.label: Document requirements computed server-side from the candidate's answers
nodes.norm_label: document requirements computed server-side from the candidate's answers
nodes.rationale: Today requiredDocuments() lives hard-coded in the frontend, so nothing is actually required by any server.

nodes.label: Automatic suspension lifts on deposit, not on review
nodes.norm_label: automatic suspension lifts on deposit, not on review
nodes.rationale: FLOW-01 section 7 promises the only unattended takedown is reversible immediately; the replacement document is flagged for priority review and a refusal re-suspends, so speed for the chef does not become a vetting hole.

nodes.label: Verification comes only from approval (409 DOCUMENT_REQUIRED)
nodes.norm_label: verification comes only from approval (409 document_required)
nodes.rationale: Every candidate holds a chef profile, so the admin flag endpoint must refuse isVerified until approval, otherwise it skips the document check; approval itself is refused unless every blocking document is valid.

nodes.label: Contact details masked when served, not when stored
nodes.norm_label: contact details masked when served, not when stored
nodes.rationale: messages.body is always what was written; a detected phone or email is served masked and the conversation flagged for admins, who read the original; regex detection is deterrence, not a guarantee.

nodes.label: Env precedence: repo-root .env.local overrides shell exports
nodes.norm_label: env precedence: repo-root .env.local overrides shell exports
nodes.rationale: Exporting SUPABASE_DB_URL or CLERK_SECRET_KEY does not redirect the sync scripts, which can reach hosted Postgres while you believe you are on localhost; check the printed Database line before writing.

nodes.label: GET /bookings returns every booking (no admin guard)
nodes.norm_label: get /bookings returns every booking (no admin guard)

nodes.label: Explicit owner rule in every module reading meals
nodes.norm_label: explicit owner rule in every module reading meals
nodes.rationale: Admin meals and menu-weeks touch Lab's Food rows only; /menus/current and the client booking detail drop ingredients and steps; admin topMeals keeps Lab's Food meaning; shopping lists count every booked dish whoever owns it; quotes never read meals.

nodes.label: Extend meals into the chef-owned dish (no second table)
nodes.norm_label: extend meals into the chef-owned dish (no second table)
nodes.rationale: meals already carries ~80% of the fields and booking_meals references it; with one table a suspended dish stays resolvable for prestations already booked, with two a booking would reference either table.

nodes.label: Recipes never exposed publicly (section 8)
nodes.rationale: Ingredients and steps are the chef's craft, handed to the client after the prestation and to admins for review, never on the vitrine.

nodes.label: meals.chef_profile_id (owner, Cascade) and created_by_user_id (author, SetNull)
nodes.rationale: Cascade on the owner because nulling it would turn a chef's dish into a public Lab's Food suggestion, while booking_meals RESTRICT still blocks deleting a booked dish; SetNull on the author because content outlives its author. Additive migration: existing rows become Lab's Food meals.

nodes.label: Known pre-existing issues: lint errors in src/generated, registerClient TTL test
nodes.norm_label: known pre-existing issues: lint errors in src/generated, registerclient ttl test

nodes.label: One access rule: 404 on read, 403 CONTENT_NOT_OWNED on write
nodes.norm_label: one access rule: 404 on read, 403 content_not_owned on write
nodes.rationale: ChefContentService applies one rule on every chef path; another chef's row is 404 on reads so a chef cannot probe other chefs' ids; admin and public reads bypass it; the section 8 access table is one test across every actor.

nodes.label: A chef never reads or copies another chef's content
nodes.norm_label: a chef never reads or copies another chef's content
nodes.rationale: Section 8 already withholds a recipe from every non-owner chef; this extends the rule to copying. The public vitrine is unaffected because its fields are public and never carry a recipe.

nodes.label: Ownership (chef_profile_id) separate from authorship (created_by_user_id)
nodes.rationale: Conflating them would make whoever typed a row its owner; an admin editing Lab's Food content must not lock it, any admin may edit it; created_by_user_id is attribution only; ownership changes only through the chef's own act (create, adopt, accept), never an admin write.

nodes.label: PRD: Brevo email templates (HTML sources, safety tests, editing workflow)
nodes.norm_label: prd: brevo email templates (html sources, safety tests, editing workflow)

nodes.label: Sign-in link emailed only, never in the HTTP response
nodes.norm_label: sign-in link emailed only, never in the http response
nodes.rationale: Email-ownership proof: the Clerk user has no password, so the inbox is the only way in; submitting someone else's address creates an account nobody can open. The link moves from approval to submission rather than disappearing.

nodes.label: Transactional email via Brevo hosted templates (BREVO_TPL_* ids as config)
nodes.norm_label: transactional email via brevo hosted templates (brevo_tpl_* ids as config)
nodes.rationale: French candidate-facing copy including refusal reasons; wording can change without a backend deploy; template ids become configuration.

nodes.label: No template engine (EJS, Handlebars, Pug rejected)
nodes.norm_label: no template engine (ejs, handlebars, pug rejected)
nodes.rationale: Brevo already renders params at send time, so a Node engine would only assemble static HTML at build time with a second language and second escaping model; Handlebars collides with Brevo's {{ }}; adds a dependency.

nodes.label: Six node:test template security rules
nodes.rationale: Attacker-typed text from the public candidature form reaches admin inboxes; rules: params within the declared list, no |safe or autoescape off or raw, href only from *Url params or https/mailto, user-controlled vars never inside attributes, sign-in templates contain signInUrl, build takes no runtime data.

nodes.label: upload.mjs --check / --update / --force (repo as source of truth)
nodes.rationale: The old upload skipped templates by name, so edits silently never reached Brevo; --check is a read-only drift report, --update pushes subject and htmlContent only and refuses to overwrite a Brevo-side edit without --force.

nodes.label: Upload digest comment (sha256 of subject and whitespace-collapsed HTML)
nodes.norm_label: upload digest comment (sha256 of subject and whitespace-collapsed html)
nodes.rationale: Lives in each Brevo account (staging and prod keep their own), no lock file to commit, stripped at send; a template tag was rejected because it would split send statistics per version.
nodes.label: Return the authenticated Clerk user's identifiers (protected sample route).
nodes.norm_label: return the authenticated clerk user's identifiers (protected sample route).
